title: Evidence for Chapter 28: the Great Depression in the United States, 1929-1936
source: Franklin D. Roosevelt's fireside chat of 12 March 1933, Proclamations 2039, 2040 and 2072, Executive Order 6102 and the White House statement of 31 January 1934 (the American Presidency Project); the Statutes at Large (47 Stat. 56, 48 Stat. 1, 48 Stat. 162, 48 Stat. 337; govinfo); the Federal Reserve Bulletin (February 1933, February 1937, September 1937); Fisher (1933, Econometrica); Bernanke (1983, NBER Working Paper 1054); Romer (NBER Working Papers 2639 and 3829); Bordo, Redish and Rockoff (NBER Working Paper 17312); Bernanke's remarks of 8 November 2002; Federal Reserve History's essays; the Canada Year Book 1934-35; the authority records of the Bibliothèque nationale de France and the Library of Congress
series: Evidence rows: id, place, year, values (';' separated, in the order of the quotation), unit, source key, page or document, the source text verbatim (empty for a value read on a page image), note
license: Quotations for criticism, scholarship and teaching, each with its source; no full original is redistributed. Works of the United States government are in the public domain: the presidential speech, proclamations, executive order and White House statement, the Statutes at Large, the Federal Reserve Bulletin, and the remarks of Governor Bernanke (Board of Governors). The American Presidency Project asks for the credit 'Online by Gerhard Peters and John T. Woolley, The American Presidency Project' (row fdr_credit). Federal Reserve History's essays are quoted in short phrases with their source. Fisher (1933): 'Copyright 1933 by the Econometric Society.' (row fis_copyright); short phrases only. NBER Working Papers 1054 (Bernanke 1983), 2639 (Romer 1988) and 3829 (Romer 1991) print no copyright line; they are quoted in short phrases with their source. NBER Working Paper 17312: '© 2011 by Michael D. Bordo, Angela Redish, and Hugh Rockoff. All rights reserved. Short sections of text, not to exceed two paragraphs, may be quoted without explicit permission provided that full credit, including © notice, is given to the source.' (row brr_copyright). The Canada Year Book 1934-35 (Dominion Bureau of Statistics, 1935) is out of Crown copyright. The authority records of the Bibliothèque nationale de France (data.bnf.fr) are metadata reused under the Licence Ouverte (Open License); the Library of Congress name authorities (id.loc.gov) are public data. The chapter's Chinese renders the quotations; the translations are the book's.
notes: Every quotation is checked word for word against the cached source text by data/fetch/verify_web_quotes.py, and every value is read from its quotation by checks/check_ch28.py; rows with an empty quotation are values read on a page image (sources nberw1054img and frb1937sepimg), named as such in their notes. OCR misprints are kept in the quotations and named in the notes (Bernanke 1983: '(11.1)', '(11.2)' and '(p.1)' for equations (4.1), (4.2); the Bulletin of September 1937: 14,948 for 14,943 and a number broken at a line end; Romer 1991: 'Ml', 'CUP', '[1933-1941)'; Fisher: 'Irvine FIsHEer', 'réle'). Indirect testimony: Harrison's message of 1 March 1933 (through George S. Eccles 1982, as reported by Federal Reserve History), Hoover's memoirs (1952), Meltzer (2003), Chandler (1971), Wicker (1996), Temin (1976), Clark (1933), Brown (1956), Kryzanowski and Roberts (1993) and Friedman and Schwartz (1963), whose book was not obtained: their argument is given through Bernanke (2002) and Federal Reserve History. Wheelock (1992) could not be downloaded (the St. Louis Fed's servers failed on 2026-10-22). The annual figures are in depressionus_annual; real GDP and the GDP deflator are Chapter 2's bea_nipa_annual.
